text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government has announced a seven-point package of generous tax concessions for the value-added textile sectors for boosting exports.
- Wheat sowing in Punjab province is facing serious problems mainly due to indifferent attitude of the government machinery towards the largest cash crop, growers say.

- The government has curtailed several perks and privileges of employees and executives of government-run banks and development finance insitutions besides merging the Rice Export Corporation and Cotton Export Corporation into the Trading Corporation of Pakistan.
- The Punjab provincial government has decided to levy tax on landholdings above 12.5 acres.
- The Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd is proposing to clamp a five-minute limit for a local call, after which a second call would be charged.
- Nineteen people were injured when a bomb explosion rocked Karachi's central business district. BUSINESS RECORDER
- The caretakers have decided to re-formulate election laws to make the electoral system an extension of accountability.
- Punjab province's former chief minister Arif Nakai has challenged the dismissal of the Punjab Assembly.

- The Supreme Court declared that the prime minister's advice is binding on the president in the appointment of superior court judges as long as it is within the parameters laid down by the March 20 judgement.

- Deposed prime minister Benazir Bhutto wrote two letters to President Farooq Leghari to protest at the "inhuman, barbaric and brutal treatment" of her husband Asif Ali Zardari and at the interim government's intention to sign long-term agreementswith the International Monetary Fund.
- Pakistan Muslim League leader Nawaz Sharif held his first meeting with President Farooq Leghari since the dismissal of Benazir Bhutto's government on November 5.

- High-level official talks between India and Pakistan are to open on December 17 in New Delhi, with caretaker Foreign Minister Sahibzada Yaqub Khan and Foreign Secretary Najmuddin Sheikh heading the Pakistani delegation.
